newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger sees progress in next two weeks.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger sees progress in next two weeks.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger said on Sunday he expected some progress on forming a government in the next two weeks.
But the president of his conservative National Party, Geoff Thompson, said the outcome may not be clear before parliament reconvenes on December 13.

Bolger told reporters in his home constituency of Te Kuiti: "I'm sure we will see some progress in the next two weeks, but that may not be final...We shouldn't presume that what takes European countries weeks or sometimes months we can do in hours or days."

Bolger will continue as caretaker prime minister in the interim. "Any issue of significance...will be dealt with in consultation with other parties. I do not anticipate any difficulty governing New Zealand for whatever the period is until the government is formed," he said.
He said cabinet would meet on Monday to discuss what policy issues needed dealing with in the next few weeks, and the National Party parliamentary caucus would meet on Tuesday.
Thompson said National was not putting any time frame on when New Zealand First Party leader Winston Peters, who holds the balance of power between National and Labour, should make his mind up.

"I think Mr Peters is in such a strong position, there is no reason for him to be rushed. Any of the main parties would be foolish to tip their hand too quickly as things mature," he said. -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
